structure.title: HBM moves more data, faster
structure.subtitle: DQ count (left axis) and DQ speed (right axis) · HBM through HBM5
structure.source: Samsung · PHY IO in B-die · Hot Chips 2026

hardToReadAreas: Marker labels are not printed. HBM4E and HBM5 speed anchors are explicit; the other speed points are source-visible axis readings.

trend.description: DQ count steps up at HBM4 while DQ speed rises steadily toward HBM5.

volatility.description: Speed makes the largest step from HBM4E to HBM5; DQ count stays flat after HBM4.

narrative.subMessage: DQ count doubles at HBM4, while speed reaches 23.5Gbps at HBM5.
narrative.headline: HBM moves more data, faster
narrative.summary: DQ is the path that lets data move in and out. Tracking both path count and per-path speed makes the generation change easier to understand.
narrative.story: Think of a highway. DQ count is the number of lanes, and DQ speed is how fast cars can travel in one lane. HBM4 takes the lanes from 1024 to 2048, while HBM5 raises per-lane speed to 23.5Gbps.
keyTakeaways: DQ count stays at 1024 from HBM through HBM3E in the source-visible chart.
DQ count reaches 2048 at HBM4 and stays there through HBM5.
DQ speed is 16Gbps for HBM4E and 23.5Gbps for HBM5.
narrative.viewerAction: Separate the left and right units, then compare the HBM4 count jump with the HBM5 speed jump.
contextualNotes: Samsung · PHY IO in B-die · Hot Chips 2026
HBM4E = 16Gbps and HBM5 = 23.5Gbps are explicit input anchors.

focusPoint.reason: The latest explicit speed anchor shows the faster data path.
